confirm.text: These are multi-select entries on the air job and OWL forms. Kelby Hammer confirmed on 09/23 that flagging them is correct and that this is a training issue rather than a record of events. None of them should be treated as a confirmed stop-work event without asking the technician. Read the exact item selected: "Stop work authority was discussed" is a routine pre-job item, not an exercise of authority.
Important caveat on today's figures. Jacob Hernandez, closing job 36074 at Driver B37 10-15H 308H, entered this in the OWL "One thing we'll do better next time" field:
"Stop work utilized is not an option to be ticked. Please advise"

If the "Stop work authority utilized" option cannot in fact be selected in the field app, then the fact that it was chosen on zero forms today tells us nothing, and the same would apply to earlier days. This needs a check of the StreetSmart form configuration and a reply to Hernandez before any conclusion is drawn from the stop-work selections.
Selected "Stop work authority was discussed" and also "Unsafe conditions" (6 forms):

Jimmy White — XTO, Shauna 9-16-16A 1H, job 36091_1. Narrative does describe a real event: "crew had wrong parts for part of the conversion. Had to shutdown and wait for new parts to be brought out." See the separate note below.
1099 William Jimmy Cooper — XTO, XBC Giddings Estate 5D HWD, job 36135. No narrative describes any unsafe condition; the free text reads "Crews working safely" and "Crews performed job safely".
Ralph Forbes — XTO, XBC Giddings Estate 5D HWD, job 36134. Narrative: "Set up exclusion zone to remove fiberglass pipes and replace".
1099 Gage Gonzales — XTO, Donovan 2U 121H, job 36131. Narrative: "WAME, Breaking Containment, mechanical lifting".
Raymundo Solis — XTO, Hernandez 20 #1, job 36004. Narrative: "Exclusion zone was set up at the entrance".
1099 Kedrick McCarter — XTO, Hernandez 20 #1, job 36005. Narrative: "Hold point used once we stopped pumping down the well to sue the crane".

Selected "Stop work authority was discussed" with no unsafe-conditions item (18 forms): Jerry Gonzales (36130, 36136, and 36058 from 10/21), 1099 Gage Gonzales (36137), Dawson Drake (36132, 36138), Jeremy Norris (36078, 36114), 1099 Bobby Galindo (36079, 36115), Jacob Hernandez (36074, 36116), Bryan Medlin (36118, 36120), Alexander Clubb (36146_1), Tyrell Sanders (36146_2, first of two OWLs), Michael Jobe (36122), Luis Zarate (36076).
Not the mis-selection pattern — these four read differently and are worth separate attention.

Jimmy White, job 36091_1 at Shauna 9-16-16A 1H: the narrative names an actual work stoppage, yet "Suspended Time" on the job record is blank and Time On Job equals Total Job Time. Either the stoppage was not logged as a suspension or the narrative overstates it — worth one question to White.

1099 William Jimmy Cooper, job 36135 at XBC Giddings: he selected "Unsafe conditions" and also answered "Did we leave the location better than we found it?" with "No", explaining "Same as on arrival". The No is probably a literal reading of the question rather than a problem, but paired with an unexplained "Unsafe conditions" selection it is worth confirming.

Michael Jobe, job 36122 at McMaster 04, is the inverse case: his narrative names a real condition while "Unsafe conditions" was not selected — "Got here to location in they didn't want us to use the road so had to drive with the MT in the woods". An access restriction that put a vehicle off-road is worth capturing properly.

Ruben Rojo, job 35950 at MABEE 7E 5H, is a different problem entirely: the multi-select is empty, the whole OWL Learn section is blank, the recorded job duration is one minute, "Details if Any" reads "Job was canceled", and the 10/22 board lists Rojo as DAYS OFF. This is a form filed against a cancelled 10/19 job, not a stop-work item.

Repeat appearances: Michael Jobe and Nathan Contreras have both appeared on this list on earlier days. Contreras filed no OWL form today, because the SM Energy air job type he works does not carry one. Jobe did select a stop-work item today but did not select "Unsafe conditions", which is a change from 09/26 when he selected it twice in one day.

Trailer forms of both kinds, and the equipment sections of the H2S daily, are photo-based. A defect visible only in a photograph would not surface in this review. Fire extinguisher inspection and expiration dates, first aid kit dates and 4-gas calibration dates exist only inside images, not as text, so this review can confirm that a photo was taken and when it was taken, but not what it shows. Separately, this run was executed at 11:00 PM Central on the day being reviewed, so the usual second pass over the following morning for late-arriving submissions was not possible. Any form for 10/22 that lands after midnight Central is not included here.
